title: Alibaba's Qwen3.8-Max-0902 Coding Update Tops Code Arena WebDev, Edging Out Claude Opus 5 Max
detail: Alibaba released Qwen3.8-Max-0902 on September 2, a post-training snapshot upgrade to its flagship Qwen3.8-Max model focused specifically on coding and long-horizon agent tasks. The underlying architecture is unchanged — 2.4 trillion total parameters, a 1-million-token context window, and the same $2/$6 per-million-token API pricing — but Alibaba said all eight tracked coding benchmarks improved, with the largest gains on TerminalBench 3.0 (11.3 to 29.0) and ProgramBench Almost Solved (10.5 to 28.0), both more than doubling. On the Code Arena WebDev leaderboard, Qwen3.8-Max-0902 ranked first overall with 1,691 points, narrowly ahead of Anthropic's Claude Opus 5 Max (1,687), Moonshot's Kimi K3 Max (1,674), and its own predecessor Qwen3.8-Max (1,669). The release extends the rapid-iteration pattern among Chinese AI labs — Alibaba, DeepSeek, Moonshot, Zhipu, and Tencent have all shipped major open-weight model updates within the past two weeks as competition intensifies for share of the coding-agent market.

title: Tencent-Backed AI Chipmaker Enflame Opens Shanghai STAR Market IPO Subscription, Targeting $911M at ~$9B Valuation
detail: Enflame Technology, a Shanghai-based AI chipmaker majority-customer-backed by Tencent, opened subscriptions on September 2 for its Shanghai STAR Market IPO, pricing shares at 142.18 yuan (~$21.15) each and targeting roughly 6.12 billion yuan (~$911 million) in proceeds at an implied valuation near 61.2 billion yuan (~$9 billion). Tencent, which accounted for 83.8% of Enflame's 2025 revenue and holds about 20.3% of the company including related parties, took a strategic placement allocation worth roughly 248 million yuan. Enflame is the last of China's four closely watched 'little dragon' GPU startups — after Moore Threads, MetaX and Biren Technology — to reach public markets, and differentiates itself with a domain-specific-architecture (DSA) chip design aimed at AI inference rather than general-purpose GPU competition with Nvidia. The retail portion of the offering drew extraordinary demand, oversubscribed more than 4,000 times as Chinese investors continued piling into the AI-chip IPO wave that has already delivered blockbuster debuts for CXMT and Unitree Robotics this year.
